item.title: Netanyahu suggests other officials to blame for Oct. 7 failings
item.description: TEL AVIV, Israel — Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of Israel has repeatedly refused to take direct responsibility for the security and intelligence failings that occurred on his watch in the lead-up to the Hamas-led attacks of Oct. 7, 2023, the bloodiest day in the country’s history.

item.title: Besides stars and stripes, a few new flags are flying in Greenland
item.description: For years, the United States was the only major country to run a full-time consulate in Greenland, and it isn’t much — a little red house with an American flag poking out.

item.title: The difference that ICE watchers are making in Minnesota
item.description: In the months leading up to the 2024 election, Jill Garvey, an organizer in Chicago for liberal advocacy groups, gathered with some like-minded colleagues and, she recalled, “did some scenario planning.”

item.title: Trump deletes racist video of Obamas after outcry
item.description: WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump posted a blatantly racist video clip portraying former President Barack Obama and former first lady Michelle Obama as apes, then deleted it after an unusually strong and public outcry from members of his own party.

item.title: Iran is at work on missile and nuclear sites, satellite images show
item.description: Iran appears to have rapidly repaired several ballistic missile facilities damaged in strikes last year, but it has made only limited fixes to major nuclear sites struck by Israel and the United States, a New York Times analysis of satellite imagery suggests.

item.title: How to tell if you will save money using TrumpRx
item.description: The government website TrumpRx.gov gives Americans a new option for getting their medications. But it also adds to the complexity of a system that can make it extraordinarily difficult for people to compare prices and figure out where to find the least expensive drug.

item.title: Tropical Gardening: Adventures in nature, conservation and diverse cultures with the International Palm Society
item.description: Members of the International Palm Society and Hawaii Island Palm Society are about to embark on an adventure from Vietnam to Thailand studying the palms of those regions. Some members are extending the trip to include some remote islands like the Andaman and Nicobar Islands in the Bay of Bengal.

item.title: Plant of the Month for February 2026: Japanese Flowering Cherry Tree
item.description: In early February, the flowering of Japanese cherry trees marks the beginning of spring in Hawaii. Today, the annual Waimea Cherry Blossom Festival is celebrating these trees and the ancient Japanese tradition of flower viewing.

item.title: Inside Patriots-Seahawks Super Bowl matchup: What to watch when Seattle has the ball
item.description: Quarterback Sam Darnold answered the questions about whether he can perform in a big game with the best performance of his life in the Seattle Seahawks’ NFC Championship Game win. He saw the game so clearly, knew exactly what the Los Angeles Rams defense was doing and punished them from the start of the game to the end.
